rules.title: New Jersey Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about criminal history on applications or orally or in writing before making a conditional offer. They may never consider non-conviction, expunged, sealed, pardoned, vacated or juvenile records. After an offer they may consider only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods, and any withdrawal needs written reasons and an individualized assessment.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer
rules.key_value: No criminal-history inquiry before conditional offer; look-back 6 yrs (1st degree), 4 yrs (2nd/3rd), 1 yr (4th)
rules.effective_date_note: Computed: approved June 18, 2021; effective first day of the seventh month next following enactment.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000, $5,000, or $10,000 depending on prior violations; enforced via Division on Civil Rights; director may order return of application fee and up to $1,000 to applicant.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot refuse to rent or discriminate based on source of lawful income or source of lawful rent payment, such as a Section 8 voucher.
rules.quoted_span: The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses
rules.key_value: Ban on source-of-income discrimination (incl. Section 8 vouchers)
rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment in an owner-occupied two-family dwelling; rooms in an owner-occupied one-family home; religious organization preference.
rules.penalty: Up to $10,000 for a first offense

unverifiable_exemptions: room rental in owner-occupied one-family dwelling

rules.review_note: Section 10:5-12 is identified in D067; D068 does not give a section. No effective date in documents.

rules.title: NJ residential rental application fee cap ($50)
rules.requirement: Landlords or their agents cannot charge an application or similar fee above $50 to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental. The cap is adjusted annually for CPI, and wrongly charged amounts are refunded to the applicant.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50
rules.effective_date_note: Computed: first day of the fourth month following approval on January 20, 2026.
rules.exemptions: One-family or two-family dwellings; NJ Real Estate Commission licensees unless they are the landlord.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 first offense, $750 second, $1,000 each subsequent; wrongly charged amount remitted to applicant

unverifiable_exemptions: licensee of the NJ Real Estate Commission who is not the landlord

rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Law – cap, handling, interest and return
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit above 1.5 times one month's rent, and yearly increases may not exceed 10%. Prepaid rent counts toward the cap (max 2.5 months at lease start including first month). Deposits are held in trust in an interest-bearing NJ account, and must be returned with interest less itemized deductions within 30 days after the tenancy ends; wrongful withholding can cost double damages.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent; annual increase max 10%; return within 30 days
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant sends a written request; interest rules do not apply to seasonal rentals.
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongfully withheld plus costs and attorney's fees; $500-$2,000 civil penalty for willful withholding from assisted tenants

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in by written request)

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act (good cause, notices, grounds)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict or fail to renew a residential lease without good cause listed in the Anti-Eviction Act. Except for nonpayment, a written Notice to Quit (often after a Notice to Cease) is required, with notice periods from 3 days to 3 years depending on the ground; self-help evictions are illegal. Owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings have separate rules (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2). Landlords who evict to occupy must occupy 6 months; removal from residential use carries a 5-year bar and penalties (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.6). Rent increases need a notice to quit and notice of increase.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause
rules.key_value: Good cause required; Notice to Quit 3 days to 3 years depending on ground
rules.effective_date_note: Only the session law year is available (P.L.1974, c.49, named in D065).
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units (two-three unit owner-occupied); transient/seasonal hotel and motel guests; unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.
rules.penalty: Illegally evicted tenant may recover possession and damages including fees; treble damages and up to $10,000 civil penalty for certain violations.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units
unit held in trust for developmentally disabled family member

rules.title: NJ reprisal (retaliation) protections for tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict, substantially alter lease terms, or refuse to renew a lease because a tenant enforced rights, made a good-faith complaint to authorities, joined a tenant organization, or refused retaliatory lease changes. The tenant may sue for damages.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights
rules.key_value: Ban on retaliatory eviction, lease alteration or non-renewal

rules.title: NJ Foreclosure Fairness Act tenant protections
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. A buyer who wants to occupy the unit must give a 90-day notice to quit after any lease ends. New owners must send tenants notices within 10 business days and may not pressure tenants to accept buyout offers.
rules.quoted_span: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction in New Jersey
rules.key_value: 90-day notice to quit; notice within 10 business days of sale
rules.review_note: Applies only to units whose property was foreclosed.

rules.title: NJ bar on rent increases to cover condominium conversion costs
rules.requirement: After conversion to a condo, co-op or fee simple ownership, rents may not be increased to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Increases for new services or amenities are allowed.
rules.quoted_span: rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion

requires_unknown_facts: building converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not pay for or use a coordinator's algorithmic pricing software or device that performs a coordinating function, and no one may perform a coordinating function or engage in parallel pricing coordination for residential rents. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act.
rules.quoted_span: a rental property owner, or any agent, representative, or subcontractor thereof, to receive, subscribe to, contract for, or otherwise exchange any form of consideration in return for the use of, the services of a coordinator;
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting coordination using nonpublic competitor data
rules.effective_date_note: Computed: first day of the twelfth month next following enactment (approved 2026-07-20); D060 also states July 1, 2027.
rules.exemptions: Research/statistical use not used to set prices, free public rent estimates, equal-terms brokerage databases, government affordability controls; excludes inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, detention facilities.
rules.penalty: Violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act (remedies in P.L.1970, c.73 §§6-17); AG complaint portal.
rules.interaction: Section 6(b) bars municipal ordinances that conflict with the act.
rules.conflict_note: Section 6(b) prohibits conflicting municipal ordinances, so once effective it may preempt Jersey City and Hoboken algorithmic rent ordinances; flag for review.

unverifiable_exemptions: inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, detention or correctional facilities

no_rule_findings.finding: New Jersey has no state law that establishes, governs or caps rents; rent control is left to municipal ordinances.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents

dropped_candidates.reason: New-construction exemption from local rent control (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5) only limits local rules; expressed in city rules' coverage, not a state rule of its own.
Narrow condo-conversion protected tenancy; covered within the Anti-Eviction Act conversion grounds, not kept as a principal law from a broad guide.
